questions.q:
p = (3 over −2) and q = (−1 over 5).
Find 2p − q as a column vector.
ms: M1: 2p = (6 over −4) or one component correct
questions.tip: Write column vectors with the numbers one above the other and no comma.

questions.q:
u = (7 over −24).
Find |u|, the magnitude of u.
questions.tip: Square the negative component in a bracket: (−24)² = 576.

questions.q:
A is the point (−1, 4) and B is the point (3, 1).
(a) Write AB as a column vector. [1]
(b) Find |AB|. [1]
(c) The point C is such that AC = 3AB (as vectors). Find the coordinates of C. [2]
ms: (c) M1: 3 × their AB = (12 over −9) or adds a multiple of AB to A
questions.tip: A vector from A to B is 'B − A'; to find C, add the vector to the coordinates of A.

questions.q:
OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b (vectors).
P is the point on AB such that AP : PB = 2 : 1. M is the midpoint of OA.
(a) Find OP in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form. [2]
(b) Find MP in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form. [2]
ms: (a) M1: a + ⅔(b − a) or a correct route
(b) M1: MP = −½a + their OP or MA + AP
questions.model:
(a) AB = b − a. AP = ⅔AB = ⅔(b − a).
OP = OA + AP = a + ⅔b − ⅔a = ⅓a + ⅔b.
(b) OM = ½a, so MP = OP − OM = ⅓a + ⅔b − ½a = −⅙a + ⅔b.
questions.tip: AP : PB = 2 : 1 means AP is 2/3 of AB, not 1/2.

questions.q:
OABC is a trapezium. OA = a and OC = c (vectors).
CB is parallel to OA and CB = 2a.
M is the midpoint of AB.
(a) Find AB in terms of a and c. [1]
(b) Find OM in terms of a and c. Give your answer in its simplest form. [2]
(c) The line CB is extended to the point E so that CE = 3a. Show that O, M and E lie on a straight line. [3]
ms: (c) A1: so OM and OE are parallel and share the point O, so O, M and E are collinear
questions.model:
(a) AB = AO + OC + CB = −a + c + 2a = a + c.
(b) OM = OA + ½AB = a + ½a + ½c = (3/2)a + ½c.
(c) OE = OC + CE = c + 3a.
OM = ½(3a + c) = ½OE.
OM is a multiple of OE, so they are parallel, and both lines pass through O. So O, M and E are collinear.
questions.tip: To prove collinearity you need two things: one vector is a multiple of the other, AND they share a point.

questions.q:
OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b (vectors).
P is the point on OA such that OP = ⅔a. Q is the midpoint of AB.
R is the point on OB extended such that OR = kb, where k is a number.
P, Q and R lie on a straight line.
(a) Find PQ in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form. [2]
(b) Write down PR in terms of a, b and k. [1]
(c) Find the value of k. [3]
ms: (a) M1: PQ = −⅔a + a + ½(b − a) or OQ − OP with OQ = ½a + ½b
(c) M1: PR = λ PQ (PR is a multiple of PQ)
(c) M1: compares coefficients of a: −⅔ = −λ/6 giving λ = 4
questions.model:
(a) OQ = ½a + ½b. PQ = OQ − OP = ½a + ½b − ⅔a = −⅙a + ½b.
(b) PR = OR − OP = −⅔a + kb.
(c) P, Q, R collinear, so PR = λ PQ:
−⅔a + kb = λ(−⅙a + ½b)
a terms: −⅔ = −λ/6 → λ = 4
b terms: k = 4 × ½ = 2.
questions.tip: Compare the coefficients of a and of b separately: each gives one equation.
